Allocation proof:

- HashMap reported capacity 448, entries are 64 bytes, and the map struct is 48 bytes on this build. The stated 512-bucket estimate is approximately 32 KiB of entries plus 62,208 bytes of text and small control/allocation overhead: about 100 KB is a reasonable retained-repeat-table budget, not an allocator-independent exact RSS limit. It does not purport to bound input buffers or transient full-line processing.
- remembered_lines_are_bounded_in_allocated_bytes passed and now tests stored capacity, including UTF-8 truncation. This encodes the round-1 harness lesson in the correct deterministic sensor.

Lock-loop cost:
- daemon_log.rs:84-86 calls Shared::sync at startup. write_line's per-line check calls it only when the accumulated output reaches the cap (267-274). Rotation::sync acquires the lock (455-458); no other production acquisition exists.
- The new loop is bounded contention retry, not a periodic background poll: 200 nonblocking flock attempts with a 10-ms in-process sleep after each EWOULDBLOCK (485-505). One open/close per acquisition sequence; one flock when uncontended, up to 200 under contention. Zero process launches, no timer/tick/seat multiplicative work.
- Private scratch probe: continuously held lock returned Busy after 2,666.008 ms; uncontended lock took 80.083 us. The 200 x 10 ms is a nominal sleep budget, not a two-second wall-clock deadline, because syscall/scheduler delays add to it. While contending, the logger's shared mutex is held, so output processing can pause for this bounded sequence; this happens only at startup/cap, not every ordinary line.
- Busy/error handling resets the accumulated cap counter, so it does not immediately retry on the next line. Normal rotation remains metadata operations at 16 MiB, with startup oversize copying only the tail, not the whole historic file.
- The lock and recheck are BRAKES on destructive rotation. Size-based trimming/dropping remains a destructive POLICY. Independent correctness/security roles own the requested race, crash and path judgments.
